# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**Reese Mercado**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-01**
- **Member name:** Reese Mercado
- **Member ID:** W529317483
- **Reference number:** POC-8AD74FF769-66861
- **Requested service:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
- **Requesting surgeon:** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), State of Arizona

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) and asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. The notice dated August 1, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already in Cigna's hands meet the plan's own published imaging criteria.

The policy I am relying on is the one that governs this request: **Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 (Partial Knee Replacement section)**, available at:
https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replac%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

### 1. Imaging findings

The plan's policy states:

> "Imaging or arthroscopic findings show EITHER of the following:"

> "severe unicompartmental (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral) osteoarthritis as evidenced by ANY of the following:"

One of the findings the policy lists under that heading is:

> "Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV radiographic findings"

My records establish exactly that. My MRI of the knee dated June 8, 2026 documents **full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially**. That is disease in a single compartment — the medial compartment — and it is reported at the grade the policy names by name.

The policy's list of qualifying imaging findings also includes:

> "Outerbridge Classification Grade IV arthroscopic findings AND not a candidate for joint sparing procedure"

> "Modified Outerbridge Classification Grade IV MRI findings AND not a candidate for joint sparing procedure"

> "unicompartmental avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral condyles and/or proximal tibia"

Because the criterion is written as "ANY of the following," meeting the Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV item is sufficient on its own. My imaging report states that finding in those terms.

The denial notice tells me the imaging did not support medical necessity, but it does not tell me which imaging criterion Cigna applied or what about the June 8, 2026 MRI it found insufficient. If the reviewer read the MRI differently than it is written, I would ask that the report be re-read alongside this letter.

### 2. Physical exam

The plan's policy states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings:"

and includes among those findings:

> "knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) >90º"

My exam documents **positive provocative testing on the affected side** and **range of motion limited by pain**. My chart as submitted does not record my arc of motion in degrees. I am asking my surgeon's office to supply that measurement, and I ask that Cigna accept it as a supplement to this appeal: **[measured knee arc of motion in degrees, from Dr. Lindqvist's office]**. This excerpt of the policy introduces a second exam finding that I was not given the text of, so I cannot address it point by point; I ask Cigna to identify that criterion and state whether it was a basis for the denial.

### 3. Symptoms

The plan's policy states:

> "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:"

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"

> "loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My records document **24 months of progressive pain in the knee, unrelieved by rest** — two full years of symptoms. They also document that I **cannot climb stairs without assistance** and that I **wake 3–4 times nightly with pain**. Being unable to manage stairs on my own, and losing sleep every night, is loss of knee function interfering with ordinary daily activities.

If Cigna needs my walking distance stated in the terms the policy uses, my surgeon's office can provide it: **[documented walking distance before pain limits me]**.

### 4. Non-surgical management

The plan's policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My records show provider-directed, non-surgical care that failed:

- **Supervised physical therapy** focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, **8 weeks from 2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07, 24 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **NSAIDs for 8 months** with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18**, which gave only **3 weeks of partial relief**.

Taken together, these span well beyond three months of provider-directed non-surgical management: eight months of NSAID therapy, plus injection therapy, plus a completed 24-visit course of supervised physical therapy. Each was tried and each failed to relieve my symptoms, which is why my surgeon recommended surgery.

The policy also provides:

> "Criteria exception: Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate. The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate."

I am not relying on that exception, because I completed conservative care. I note it only to show that the policy's structure is satisfied on the primary pathway.

### 5. Preoperative optimization

The plan's policy includes this note:

> "Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities."

My records show **no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker**. I am under the care of Dr. Lindqvist, an orthopedic surgeon, who has documented that this procedure is needed.

---

## A note about the policy text I have

Several of the criteria I quoted above end with a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I was not able to obtain in full. I have quoted the policy language exactly as I have it and have not filled in anything I could not verify. **I ask Cigna to identify, in writing, the specific criterion or criteria from CMM-311 that my request was found not to meet**, so that my surgeon and I can respond to the actual basis for the decision rather than to a general statement about imaging.

---

## What I am asking Cigna to do

I respectfully ask Cigna to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-01 (reference POC-8AD74FF769-66861) and authorize CPT 27446;
2. If the denial is maintained, provide the specific CMM-311 criterion that was applied and the clinical rationale, along with the reviewing clinician's name and specialty; and
3. Advise me of any further appeal rights, including external review.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in my denial notice, which says the appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-01-28**. I am submitting it through my.cigna.com using my plan's appeal form, or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; Cigna's member line is 1-800-244-6224, or the number on my card.

Please contact me if you need any additional records. My surgeon's office can provide anything further that would help.

**Enclosures:** [MRI report dated 2026-06-08]; [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07]; [Office notes from Lindqvist, MD]; [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-01]; [Any additional records]

---

Sincerely,

**Reese Mercado**
Member ID: W529317483
[Signature]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
